title: fetchProjectTemplates $select omits dcfg_description — template line-item copy always gets undefined
detail: ProjectList.jsx line 197: `const tplLines = JSON.parse(tpl.dcfg_description);`. But fetchProjectTemplates() in portalApi.js:890 has $select=dcfg_projecttemplateid,dcfg_name,dcfg_trades,dcfg_cost_code,dcfg_base_duration_days,dcfg_bundle_flag,dcfg_isactive — dcfg_description is NOT in the $select. The server returns undefined for dcfg_description, the code checks `if (tpl?.dcfg_description)` on line 197 which is falsy, so template line copying silently does nothing. The user sees 'Project created' (line 216) instead of 'Project created with N template lines'. The entire template-to-project-lines feature is broken by the missing $select column.
evidence: portalApi.js:890 fetchProjectTemplates $select list lacks dcfg_description. ProjectList.jsx:197 reads tpl.dcfg_description.
recommendedFix: Add dcfg_description to the fetchProjectTemplates $select: `$select=dcfg_projecttemplateid,dcfg_name,dcfg_trades,dcfg_cost_code,dcfg_base_duration_days,dcfg_bundle_flag,dcfg_isactive,dcfg_description`. Per pick-lane rule, fix the consumer (the $select), not the fields-list config.

title: ProjectList initial fetchProjects .catch swallows error — no error state, no toast
detail: Line 77: `.catch(() => setLoading(false))` — if fetchProjects fails (network error, 403, etc.), loading stops but the user sees an empty table with 'No projects found' which is indistinguishable from genuinely having zero projects. Same anti-pattern as ProgramDetail CR-0284 and ContractList CR-0251.
evidence: ProjectList.jsx:77. Compare to ProgramList.jsx:30 which does set error state.
recommendedFix: Add error state: `.catch(e => { setError(e.message); setLoading(false); })` and render an error banner when error is non-null. ProgramList.jsx:34 already implements this pattern correctly.

title: Job number sequence generation uses client-side count — race condition on concurrent creates
detail: Lines 143-145: `const existing = projects.filter(p => p.dcfg_job_number?.startsWith(...)); const nextSeq = String(existing.length + 1).padStart(3, '0');`. This counts already-loaded projects in the current browser session to determine the next sequence number. If two users create projects simultaneously, or if projects were created outside the SPA, they get duplicate job numbers. Additionally, the count is based on the stale `projects` state array, not a fresh server query.
recommendedFix: Catalog-only for this review. The proper fix is server-side auto-numbering (Dataverse auto-number column or a pre-create plugin). Short-term: at minimum, re-fetch the list before generating the number, or use a timestamp-based suffix to reduce collision risk.

title: ProjectList empty-state row colSpan={6} but table has 7 columns
detail: Line 451: `<td colSpan={6}>` but the thead has 7 th elements (Job #, Project, Cost Code, Property, Trades, Est. Cost, Status). The empty-state text does not span the full table width, leaving a visual gap in the last column.
evidence: ProjectList.jsx:451 colSpan={6} vs thead row with 7 <th> elements at lines 441-448.

title: ProjectDashboard silently catches all three data fetches — no error state surfaced
detail: Lines 20-22: each of fetchPrograms(), fetchProjects(), fetchRfpPackages() has `.catch(() => ({ value: [] }))`. If ALL three fail (e.g., network down), the dashboard renders with zero data everywhere — 0 Programs, 0 Active Projects, 0 Open Bids — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty system. No error banner, no toast. A user could believe everything is fine when nothing loaded.
evidence: ProjectDashboard.jsx:20-22. All three .catch handlers return empty arrays silently.
recommendedFix: Track an error count across the three fetches. If all three fail, show an error banner. If only one fails, show a toast warning naming which section failed to load. The current pattern where individual catches return empty arrays is fine for resilience, but there should be at least a flag when all three are in error state.

title: ProjectDashboard imports budgetColor but never uses it
detail: Line 9: `import { NAVY, fmtCurrency, PROJECT_STATUS, ProjectStatus, budgetColor } from '../projectConstants.js';`. budgetColor is imported but never called anywhere in the component. fmtCurrency is also imported but never called (the dashboard only displays counts, not currency values).
evidence: ProjectDashboard.jsx:9. Grep for 'budgetColor' and 'fmtCurrency' within the file returns only the import line.
recommendedFix: Remove unused imports: change to `import { NAVY, PROJECT_STATUS, ProjectStatus } from '../projectConstants.js';`

title: ProjectDetail defines its own PROJECT_STATUS_MAP with different colors than projectConstants.js
detail: ProjectDetail.jsx lines 17-23 define a local PROJECT_STATUS_MAP with color values (#2563EB for Planned, #2D8659 for Active, #D4A017 for On Hold, #C0392B for Cancelled). projectConstants.js lines 14-20 define PROJECT_STATUS with DIFFERENT color values (#3B82F6 for Planned, #22C55E for Active, #F59E0B for On Hold, #EF4444 for Cancelled). ProjectList.jsx and ProgramDetail.jsx use the shared projectConstants version. This means status badges show different colors on the detail screen vs the list screen for the same status.
evidence: ProjectDetail.jsx:17-23 vs projectConstants.js:14-20. Planned: #2563EB vs #3B82F6, Active: #2D8659 vs #22C55E, On Hold: #D4A017 vs #F59E0B, Cancelled: #C0392B vs #EF4444.
recommendedFix: Remove the local PROJECT_STATUS_MAP from ProjectDetail.jsx and import PROJECT_STATUS from projectConstants.js instead. Adapt the rendering to use the shared map's `color` and `bg` properties.

title: deleteProjectLine uses soft-delete (dcfg_active_flag=false) but does not re-filter — deleted lines remain visible until page refresh
detail: Line 215: `await deleteProjectLine(l.dcfg_project_line_itemid);` calls apiPatch with dcfg_active_flag:false (verified in portalApi.js:897). Then line 217 calls loadLines() which fetches ALL lines including the soft-deleted one (fetchProjectLines does not filter by dcfg_active_flag eq true). The line remains in the table. The user sees 'Line removed' toast but the line is still there. It only disappears if fetchProjectLines happens to have a filter — need to verify.
recommendedFix: Verify fetchProjectLines includes `$filter=dcfg_active_flag eq true`. If it does not, add the filter. Alternatively, optimistically remove the line from local state immediately after the soft-delete succeeds, before re-fetching.

title: ProjectDetail returns null when !project after loading completes — blank screen with no feedback
detail: Line 337: `if (!project) return null;`. After loading finishes (loading=false) and there is no error but also no project data (e.g., the API returned an empty response or unexpected format), the component renders absolutely nothing. No back button, no message, no way for the user to navigate away except the browser back button.
recommendedFix:
Replace `return null` with a meaningful empty state like ProgramDetail.jsx:96 does: `

Project not found.

`. Include the back button so the user can navigate to the project list.

title: RfpDetail refresh() .catch swallows all errors — no error state, no toast on load failure
detail: Line 60: `.catch(() => setLoading(false))`. The Promise.all fetches rfpDetail, rfpProjects, rfpVendors, and proposals. If ANY of them fails, loading stops but rfp stays null, rendering 'Bid comparison not found.' (line 118) which is indistinguishable from a genuine 404. No error state, no toast. This is the same anti-pattern as ProjectList CR-1101 and ProgramDetail CR-0284.
evidence: RfpDetail.jsx:60. The catch handler has no error surfacing.
recommendedFix: Add error state and surface a toast or banner on load failure, distinguishing network/API errors from a genuine not-found.

title: RfpDetail useEffect dependency is [id] but calls refresh() which is not memoized — re-renders trigger stale closure
detail: Line 63: `useEffect(() => { refresh(); }, [id]);`. The refresh function (line 47) is declared as a plain function, not wrapped in useCallback. React's linter would flag this: refresh captures `id` via closure but isn't in the dependency array. If id changes, the effect fires but refresh still references the old id until the next render. In practice this is mostly harmless because id changes trigger a re-render, but it violates React hooks best practices and could cause subtle bugs with rapid navigation.
evidence: RfpDetail.jsx:47 (refresh declared as plain function), line 63 (useEffect depends on [id] but not refresh).
recommendedFix: Wrap refresh in useCallback with [id] dependency (matching the pattern in ProgramDetail.jsx:32 and ProjectDetail.jsx:118), then add refresh to the useEffect dependency array.

title: RfpList fetchRfpPackages .catch swallows error — no error state, no toast
detail: Line 29: `.catch(() => setLoading(false))`. Same anti-pattern as ProjectList CR-1101. On fetch failure, the list renders empty with 'No bid comparisons found.' — indistinguishable from genuinely having no data.
recommendedFix: Add error state and render an error banner, matching the pattern in ProgramList.jsx:30,34.

title: RfpList defines local NAVY constant instead of importing from projectConstants.js
detail: Line 13: `const NAVY = '#1B2A4A';`. The same constant is exported from projectConstants.js (line 6) and imported by ProgramList, ProgramDetail, ProjectDashboard, and ProjectList. RfpList duplicates it locally. Similarly, RfpDetail.jsx line 14 also defines a local NAVY. This is minor but adds maintenance drift risk if the brand color ever changes.
recommendedFix: Replace local NAVY declarations in RfpList.jsx and RfpDetail.jsx with `import { NAVY } from '../projectConstants.js';`.

title: RfpDetail status transition and edit buttons not gated by role — any user can send to vendors, award, or edit
detail: Lines 210-227: The Edit, Send to Vendors, Mark as Leveled, and Award buttons are visible to ALL users regardless of role. The isManager hook is imported (line 35) but only used for checklist toggle gating (line 378). Status transitions are business-critical workflow actions that should be restricted to managers/admins. A non-manager user can advance an RFP from Draft to Awarded with no authorization check.
evidence: RfpDetail.jsx:210-227 (no isManager guard on buttons), line 35 (isManager imported but only used at line 378).
recommendedFix: Wrap the Edit button, Send to Vendors, Mark as Leveled, and Award buttons in `{isManager() && ...}` guards, matching the pattern used for the checklist toggle at line 378.

title: ProjectDetail defines local fmtCurrency and fmtDate formatters instead of using shared projectConstants.js
detail: Lines 43-45: ProjectDetail defines `const fmtCurrency = v => v != null ? fmt.format(v) : '—';` and `const fmtDate = v => ...`. projectConstants.js exports `fmtCurrency` (line 10) with a slightly different null placeholder ('-' vs '—'). The shared fmtDate exists in portalApi.js (line 12) but is never imported. This means the same currency value renders with '-' on list screens but '—' on the detail screen.
evidence: ProjectDetail.jsx:43-44 local formatters. projectConstants.js:10 shared fmtCurrency with '-'. portalApi.js:12 shared fmtDate.
recommendedFix: Import fmtCurrency from projectConstants.js to ensure consistent null rendering. For fmtDate, either import the shared version or align the null placeholder.

title: ProgramList table rows use onClick for navigation but lack keyboard accessibility
detail: Line 67: `<tr ... onClick={() => navigate(...)}>`. Table rows have click handlers for navigation but no keyboard equivalent — no tabIndex, no onKeyDown handler for Enter/Space. A keyboard-only user cannot navigate to a program detail. Same pattern exists across ProjectList (line 459), ProjectDashboard KPI cards (line 111), ProgramDetail project rows (line 202), RfpList (line 65), and RfpDetail tables.
recommendedFix: Add `tabIndex={0}` and `onKeyDown={e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') navigate(...) }}` to all clickable table rows and cards across Programs & Projects screens. Consider using `role="link"` for semantic clarity.

title: RfpDetail local fmt currency formatter uses maximumFractionDigits:0 — inconsistent with projectConstants fmtCurrency
detail: Line 14: `const fmt = v => v != null ? new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US',{style:'currency',currency:'USD',maximumFractionDigits:0}).format(v) : '-';`. This creates a new Intl.NumberFormat instance on EVERY call (performance) AND matches projectConstants.fmtCurrency output but duplicates the logic. RfpList.jsx line 34 also defines an identical local fmt.
evidence: RfpDetail.jsx:14 and RfpList.jsx:34 both define local currency formatters. projectConstants.js:9-10 has the shared version.
recommendedFix: Import fmtCurrency from projectConstants.js in both files. Remove local fmt definitions.

title: RfpDetail Projects tab renders raw dcfg_status number instead of status label
detail: Line 306: `{proj.dcfg_status != null ? {proj.dcfg_status} : '-'}`. This displays the raw numeric enum value (e.g., '100000010') instead of the human-readable label ('Planned'). The PROJECT_STATUS map from projectConstants.js could resolve this, but RfpDetail doesn't import it.
evidence: RfpDetail.jsx:306. Compare to ProjectList.jsx:455 which uses `PROJECT_STATUS[p.dcfg_status]` for label resolution.
recommendedFix: Import PROJECT_STATUS from projectConstants.js and render the label: `const st = PROJECT_STATUS[proj.dcfg_status] || { label: String(proj.dcfg_status), cls: 'badge-grey' }; {st.label}`.
